title: Mapping Irreversible Action Patterns in Long-Horizon Agent Task Traces

original_idea.quick_reasoning: Clearly addresses an AI Safety problem with a reasonably scoped approach.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: First empirical characterization of irreversible action distribution in agent traces. Prerequisite for designing targeted safety interventions. Identifies when in a task sequence to place safety checks. Clear causal chain.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Generating or collecting agent traces from public benchmarks is feasible. Annotating each action for reversibility is structured work. Statistical analysis of patterns is accessible. Medium compute sufficient for trace generation.

narrow_scope.reasoning: 100 long-horizon traces (20+ steps each) = 2000+ action annotations. Generating the traces plus annotating all actions is very time-intensive. Would need to scope down to 30-50 traces to fit 30hrs.

novelty_assessment.reasoning: Novelty not assessed due to partial Wave 3 completion.
